Departmental Mandate

The Home Department of the Government of Maharashtra functions as the primary administrative authority responsible for the maintenance of law and order, crime prevention, and investigative oversight across the state. The department operates under the leadership of the Additional Chief Secretary (Home), overseeing critical state functions including police administration, Home Guard operations, and civil defense.

Administrative Divisions

To ensure administrative efficiency, the department is structured into specific functional sectors:

  • Law, Order, and Crime: Managed under the office of the Additional Chief Secretary (Home), this division focuses on investigation protocols and the governance of police forces.
  • Transport: Overseen by the Additional Chief Secretary (Transport), this division governs road transport and the operations of the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation.
  • Prison Administration: Managed by the Additional Chief Secretary (A & S).
  • State Excise: Supervised by the Principal Secretary (Excise).
  • Foreign Citizen Affairs: Integrated into the Home Department's jurisdiction as of December 1, 1995.

Legal Framework and Governance

The department enforces several key legislative acts to maintain public safety and protect vulnerable populations, including:

  • The Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
  • The Maharashtra Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice Act, 2013.

Public Services and Verification

The official portal of the Maharashtra Home Department serves as the central hub for administrative information and links to specialized agencies. Citizens seeking information regarding departmental notifications, state excise online services, or general administrative updates should rely exclusively on the official government domain.

For further details or to verify specific departmental updates, please visit the official website: https://home.maharashtra.gov.in/en/
